reasons: target_missing: a play names a card whose printed effects aim at ONE enemy and carries no target, so the line cannot be replayed at all
intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Jumpy Dumpty for 2 energy and then one Kaboom! with the last energy. Fwoosh! is dead on arrival because the Spark bank is empty, so my real budget is 3 energy across two Kabooms, Duck and Cover, and Jumpy Dumpty. Jumpy Dumpty is by far the best energy-for-damage in the hand: with only Nibbit on the board, 'random enemies twice' can only go one place, so it is a flat 16 now, plus a Bomb that will land 6 more later, all for 2 energy. Adding a Kaboom pushes this turn to 23 face damage on a 46 HP enemy, meaning I am halfway through it on turn one and the pending Bomb carries the rest of the way. Against a lone 46 HP body with a plain 12-damage swing and 40 HP in my pocket, I am not under any pressure that would make me want to spend energy on anything but shortening the fight.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: The line I actually weighed was Jumpy Dumpty plus Duck and Cover instead of the Kaboom: 16 damage and 5 Block, blunting the incoming 12 down to 7. I also glanced at the double-Kaboom-plus-Duck-and-Cover line for 14 damage and 5 Block, but that is strictly worse on damage than the Jumpy Dumpty opening and I dropped it quickly. The Duck and Cover version was the only one I thought about for more than a moment, and it lost on simple arithmetic: 5 Block saves exactly 5 HP once, while 7 extra damage is a fifth of the enemy's health and plausibly the difference between the fight ending in three turns instead of four. Saving a whole enemy turn is worth more than 12 HP, so trading 5 HP for that acceleration is not close.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up the 5 Block, so I take the full 12 and drop to 28 HP, and it also spends the tempo card I would otherwise be able to hold if a bigger swing shows up later. More concretely, I burned one of my two Kabooms this turn rather than keeping a spread of options for a turn where the Bomb has already gone off and I might want to line up an exact lethal. Duck and Cover is now still in hand for a later turn, which is fine, but I have effectively decided that my defensive card is a luxury and that I intend to win this by out-damaging a body that only hits for 12. If Nibbit has some on-death or on-low-HP behavior I cannot see from this page, I am walking into it at 28 HP with no Block instead of 33 with 5.
answers.q4_different_intent: Honestly, no — I could not construct an intent that flips this. A bigger telegraphed attack makes 5 Block a smaller and smaller fraction of the hit, so it argues even harder for killing faster rather than chip-mitigating; a defensive or buffing intent removes the reason for Block entirely; and a small attack makes Block pointless. Duck and Cover would only start to matter if the intent were something like a hit I could fully absorb, and 5 Block cannot fully absorb anything Nibbit is plausibly doing at this HP total. The one thing that would change the line is not the intent at all but the board: a second enemy would make Jumpy Dumpty's random targeting unreliable and might push me toward the two guaranteed Kabooms instead. Given only one enemy, the play is forced enough that I would call the decision not close.
